records.text: Val and Odyl took part in a mission to retrieve important data from a hostile ship. Odyl devised an infiltration plan that required Val to let herself be captured and tied up while Odyl acted as a double agent.

During the hostile-ship ruse, Odyl leaned close to the captured, tied-up Val, whispered “good girl” in her ear, and called her “Dearie.” Odyl then kissed Val before leaving. The planned ruse unexpectedly affected Val and set the tone for their ongoing flirtation and connection.

Val and Odyl’s hostile-ship mission succeeded and they retrieved the data. DSES-4 was angry that they had gone outside protocol and taken such a risk, but the mission’s success and Odyl’s quick thinking helped smooth matters over.

After the engine-room encounter, Val and Odyl had another brief encounter in a hallway late at night. Odyl pulled Val into a more passionate kiss, then gave her a coy smile and disappeared into the shadows. The encounter left Val breathless, wanting more, and confused about its meaning.

Val and Odyl later reunited for the Unnamed City mission on the abandoned homeworld of the Xirin, Odyl’s people. Odyl found the mission emotionally powerful and sad because of its connection to her heritage and people.

During the Unnamed City mission, Val and Odyl spent a month working closely together on challenging objectives and relying on one another. They shared hopes, fears, and vulnerable moments, and grew genuinely close as Val came to recognize Odyl’s bravery, intelligence, and loyalty to her people.

Val and Odyl spent a fiery, passionate last night together at the end of the Unnamed City mission, before being separated for a few months. Despite their intimacy, their feelings remained unspoken that night.
records.topic: last night of Unnamed City mission

A simple butternut squash soup recipe shared on 2023-05-30 serves 4–6. It calls for one 2–3 lb butternut squash, 2 tablespoons olive oil, one chopped onion, 3 minced garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon cumin, optional 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, ½ teaspoon salt, ¼ teaspoon black pepper, 4 cups chicken or vegetable broth, optional ½ cup heavy cream or coconut cream, and parsley or sage for garnish. entities: Detecting Gravitational Waves with the Moon
Detecting stochastic gravitational waves with binary resonance

records.text: The article explains that current and planned gravitational-wave detectors leave a sensitivity gap around the microhertz range, between pulsar timing arrays and future space-based interferometers such as LISA. Covering that band with an interferometer would require astronomical-scale distances, potentially comparable to the Solar System.

Diego Blas and Alexander C. Jenkins propose detecting stochastic gravitational waves by measuring their resonant effects on gravitationally bound binary systems. When a gravitational-wave frequency is an integer multiple of a binary system’s orbital frequency, the system responds resonantly; if the signal persists, the resulting orbital deviations accumulate and may become observable.

The authors suggest using the Earth–Moon system to probe the microhertz frequency range because the Moon’s orbital period is about 28 days, corresponding to an orbital frequency of roughly 10⁻⁶ Hz. Laser ranging can measure the Earth–Moon distance using retroreflectors placed on the Moon by Apollo astronauts and Soviet uncrewed landers; the distance has been measured this way for more than 50 years.

The paper estimates that measuring the Earth–Moon distance with an accuracy of approximately 0.1 millimeters could potentially reveal fluctuations caused by a microhertz stochastic gravitational-wave background, depending on the signal strength and instrument sensitivity. The authors suggest that such precision may be achievable with existing technology.

On 2023-05-30, the assistant summarized the article in Italian, explaining the microhertz detection gap and the proposal to use resonant orbital perturbations in binary systems to detect gravitational waves.
entities: Detecting Gravitational Waves with the Moon
